A bounded work queue serves as a critical synchronization mechanism in concurrent systems, primarily designed to prevent resource exhaustion by enforcing a strict limit on the number of pending tasks. When the queue reaches its maximum capacity, it effectively applies backpressure to the producer threads. Instead of allowing unbounded memory growth, which could lead to OutOfMemory errors or system instability, the queue forces the producer to either block, wait, or actively reject new submissions. This backpressure mechanism ensures that the system remains stable under load by signaling to upstream components that they are producing work faster than the downstream consumers can process it.
